newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks raise prime lending rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks raise prime lending rates.

text.p: Philippine banks raised their prime lending rates again on Tuesday after the Central Bank pushed up its term reverse repo rates, treasurers and corporate bankers polled by Reuters said on Tuesday.
They said the rates could go higher in coming days if the central bank hikes its benchmark overnight and term rates.
The central bank earlier said it would continue with its "firm monetary policy stance" despite allowing the peso to float freely, which resulted in an effective devaluation of around 11 percent.
To show it meant business, on Tuesday it increased its one-month reverse repo rate to 25 percent from 12.365 percent, a day after it offered two-week reverse repos at 25 percent.

The Philippine Commercial International Bank, one of the country's top corporate banks, quoted the highest rate at 35 percent, up from 30 percent offered late last week. It was quoting only 21 percent last Wednesday.
In June, most prime rates were in the teens.
"There was not many new deals done today and yesterday though," one corporate banker said.
The lowest rate among the big banks was quoted by Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd's Manila branch. It quoted 26 percent for its prime loans from 17.5 percent last week.
"I guess we've positioned well in the past few weeks," a loan officer said.
Banks usually set prime rates every Tuesday after the Treasury bill auction the day before. T-bill rates went up to a two-year high on Monday due to the uncertainties in the foreign exchange market.
In recent weeks, some banks were changing their prime rates almost every day.
Philippine National Bank, which is partly owned by the government, raised its prime rate to 33 percent from 20 percent, a senior treasury official said.
The prime lending rate of Bank of the Philippine Islands was at 32 percent, up from 22 percent last Friday.
Far East Bank and Trust Co was quoting 30 percent for its prime loans from 20 to 24 percent level late last week, a Far East corporate banker said.
The Philippine branch of Citibank NA, a subsidiary of Citicorp, was offering its corporate loans at 31 percent, a level which it had maintained since early last week.
Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc, the country's biggest bank, declined to give out specific rates, but a top official said it was at the low 30s.
Bankers said the rates may vary according to the credit standing of the corporate clients.
